summary: Convert account_user.referrer_id from legacy integer to ForeignKey(User) by first invalidating non-referencing values, adding the FK constraint while both versions run, then deploying the new version with state_only migration. The old version continues writing referrer_id as integer; all values reference valid users or NULL, so FK enforcement is safe. After deploy_new both versions coexist with the constrained column; retire_old removes the old version.
write_consistency: Old version writes referrer_id as integer; new version writes via Django ForeignKey. The pre-deploy SQL stage sets referrer_id to NULL for any value not present in account_user.id, preventing FK violations during concurrent operation. The note column is never modified or touched by any statement.

stages.description: Clear invalid referrer_id references to NULL, then add ForeignKey constraint referencing account_user.id.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);
ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT referrer_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id);
